notes.note: The supplied Exodus family total is seventy-five, as in the retained Genesis and Acts passages. Deuteronomy explicitly gives seventy; the retained relation identifies a parallel migration account with different totals, not an arithmetical equivalence or independent specialist reconciliation. Maternal household groupings and expanded descendants in Genesis46 retain their own order, names and source wording.

The new king is not assigned a modern historical identity or date. Preserve fortified cities Pithom, Rameses and On, which is City of the Sun, without replacing the list with store cities or proving a new modern site equivalence. The king's military fears are his reported rationale. Midwife Sepphora is not identified with Zipporah merely from similar names. The childbirth killing instruction and expanded river decree remain distinct orders.

Fear of God, refusal to kill and God's good treatment are narrated. The midwives' childbirth explanation remains reported speech, not independently verified obstetric evidence or an unquoted blanket moral ruling. Verse21 says they made houses for themselves; the agency is not replaced with God establishing their houses.

The unnamed Levite parents are linked to explicit later parental genealogies without reconstructing difficult ancestry clauses or substituting another edition's kinship and age details. The unnamed sister receives no new age or name. Preserve three months, the bitumen-pitch basket, marsh placement and Pharaoh's daughter's adoption. Wages are promised; actual payment is not separately narrated.

Stephen's action descriptions, Moses' expectation of recognition and ruler/redeemer reversal remain his retrospective account. Hebrews' faith interpretation remains a later interpretation. No independent legal verdict about the killing, invented medical account of speech, or identification of Hebrews11:27's departure with the initial flight is claimed.

Preserve the seven daughters and Jethro flock wording alongside the return to Reuel. These linked narrative units do not independently establish whether the names are alternate names, different generations or a title. Zipporah, Gershom and the later Eliezer remain as supplied. Gershom's naming explanation is Moses' reported sojourner statement, not a new language-etymology study.

The groaning, ancestral covenant remembrance and divine attention are connected without independently resolving the chronology of all royal-death notices. Verse25 says He became known to them; this is not silently replaced by He knew them. Exodus6:5 retains your covenant rather than an imported alternate pronoun.

Retain Horeb beside Stephen's Sinai label. An angel appears in the bush and the Lord speaks from it; no independent ontological identification of the appearing figure is imposed. The footwear/holy-ground command is compared with Joshua's chief captain without proving that figure's identity. The repeated Moses call and What-is-it response remain intact.

The three Gospel links are distinct actual explicit uses of the ancestral-God declaration in Jesus' resurrection teaching. Each complete retained passage was read, including the surrounding question context; their interpretive application is attributed to Jesus rather than newly derived as an independent specialist conclusion.

The good/spacious milk-and-honey land and supplied seven-peoples lists remain intact. Genesis15 has a longer land-covenant list; no exact list equivalence or new territorial border reconstruction is asserted. The later historical confession is compared on deliverance and destination.

Preserve I am the One Who Is, The One Who Is has sent me, the subsequent Lord-and-ancestral-God message, and the everlasting-name/memorial formula. The later Lord-name disclosure retains its own statement about the patriarchs. No new Hebrew/Greek collation, pronunciation, proposed etymology, or harmonization of every prior-name-knowledge statement is claimed.

The elders' commissioned petition and the later scene naming Moses and Aaron are compared without inventing unlisted participants. Retain the three-day sacrifice request, predicted resistance, strong hand, wonders, Egyptian favour and articles requested. The later source explicitly describes lending and plundering; neither a modern legal classification nor replacement terminology is added. Genesis15:14 retains much baggage.

Moses' serpent sign differs in actor, setting and supplied creature wording from Aaron's later dragon sign. The hand becomes as snow and returns to flesh colour; no leprosy label absent from the Exodus verse or modern diagnosis is inserted. Miriam's explicit leprous-as-snow description remains distinct. The poured-water sign is not equated with the later larger water judgment or given a new physical mechanism.

Preserve weak voice, slow tongue, hard-of-hearing-or-deaf wording and God's promise to open mouths. Aaron will surely speak to Moses in4:14; a fluent-speech claim is not substituted there. The distinct later powerful-in-words account and Jeremiah's youth objection are retained without forced resolution. Moses' matters-pertaining-to-God role and later a-god-to-Pharaoh wording remain distinct delegated-role statements; no ontological equation is independently inferred.

Moses returns toward Egypt with wife and children on beasts of burden. The threat-ended return pattern in Matthew has different people and the opposite destination. Israel's firstborn-son message, Ephraim's firstborn restoration title at the source's Jeremiah38:9 and Hosea's infant-Israel/plural-children wording are compared without replacing them with another numbering or a singular quotation. The release warning retains My people alongside the firstborn language.

Retain angel of the Lord, Zipporah's stone circumcision of her son, falling at the feet, and the twice-stated The blood of my child's circumcision has ceased. No bridegroom-of-blood substitution, assignment of every pronoun or foot-owner, identification of the threatened person or child, medical explanation, or unreported motive is imposed. Circumcision covenant and stone-implement parallels supply stated background, not an independently proven solution of the encounter.

Aaron meets Moses and kisses him; the inner rejoicing anticipated earlier is not separately quoted as a narrated feeling at the meeting. Moses briefs Aaron, the elders assemble, and the actual source assigns both speaking and sign performance to Aaron. The people believe and rejoice, bow and worship. The public-sign notice does not separately enumerate which conditional signs are performed.
